solutions.title: Level-order queue linking
solutions.strategy: Traverse one level at a time with a queue, wire each node to the next node in that same level, and enqueue children for the next level.

timeComplexity.explanation: Every node is enqueued, dequeued, and linked a constant number of times.

spaceComplexity.explanation: The queue can hold one tree level at once, where w is the maximum width of the tree.

solutions.title: Constant-space next-chain traversal
solutions.strategy: Use the current level's already-established next chain to build the next level's chain with a dummy tail pointer.

timeComplexity.explanation: Each node is visited once as part of a current level, and each child is appended once to the next-level chain.

spaceComplexity.explanation: The algorithm keeps only a few node pointers regardless of tree size; it mutates the existing next fields.
